domain_label: Substitutions & Dietary Adaptations (Cupcake Ingredient Selection subdomain)
assumptions: no observed dataset or benchmark evidence supplied; all scores are heuristic priors grounded in standard baking-science references
subdomain scope is principled substitution and dietary adaptation, finer than whole ingredient selection
this KB covers structure/moisture/browning/flavor tradeoffs, not dietary or medical advice
a base cupcake formula and target diet are already chosen; recipe development upstream is out of scope
exclusions: dietary or medical/nutritional advice and health claims
core mixing and baking method beyond substitution-driven adjustments
flavor development unrelated to substitution-induced shifts
cost and supply-chain sourcing beyond allergen/label verification

competency_questions.question: When is a substitution a true 1:1 drop-in versus a functional swap that needs rebalancing?
Which roles of the replaced ingredient (bulk, moisture, structure, browning) must be re-supplied?
How is a gluten-free flour blend composed to mimic wheat structure?
How much xanthan or psyllium replaces gluten without making the crumb gummy?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: GF_BINDER sets binder type and dose

competency_questions.question: When should a flax/chia egg be used instead of aquafaba?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FLAX_EGG and VEGAN_EGG split binding vs aeration roles

competency_questions.question: How is aquafaba whipped and folded to replace egg-white aeration?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: AQUAFABA defines whip endpoint and fold technique

competency_questions.question: How are butter and dairy milk swapped while preserving creaming, acidity, and browning?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PLANT_BUTTER and DAIRY_MILK match fat and restore acid/protein

competency_questions.question: How is browning restored when sugar or dairy is swapped out?
What are the structural effects of reducing total sugar and how far can it be cut?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: REDUCED_SUGAR caps the cut and lists compensations

competency_questions.question: How is moisture rebalanced after fat and sweetener swaps?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MOISTURE_SHIFT and ALT_FAT account for net hydration

competency_questions.question: How are allergen claims kept accurate down to every component?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ALLERGEN_CTRL and LABEL_DOC verify components against claims

competency_questions.question: What food-safety limits apply to raw or perishable substitutes?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FOOD_SAFETY sets heat-treatment and temperature limits

competency_questions.question: How does a chosen substitution shift structure and flavor, and how is it corrected?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: STRUCT_SHIFT and FLAVOR_SHIFT diagnose and correct shifts

competency_questions.question: How is a substituted formula validated before it is locked?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SWAP_TEST runs a control comparison and scorecard

glossary.definition: a swap that replaces an ingredient's structural roles, not just its identity, requiring rebalancing
a drop-in swap used gram-for-gram with no rebalancing
xanthan or psyllium that holds gas and water to mimic gluten in GF batter
chickpea cooking liquid whipped to replace egg-white aeration
ground-flax-and-water gel used as a binding/moistening egg replacer
a solid plant fat with butter-like fat percentage and plasticity for creaming
a sweetener or ingredient's tendency to attract and hold water, affecting moisture and shelf-life
heat-driven reaction of reducing sugars and proteins that colors and flavors cupcake tops
a sugar that participates in Maillard browning; many intense sweeteners do not
unintended transfer of an allergen from shared equipment or ingredients
available water that governs crumb moistness, staling, and spoilage

source_registry.description: heuristic prior estimates for cupcake ingredient substitution and dietary adaptation work units in absence of supplied datasets
grounding_limits: domain-general heuristic priors grounded in standard baking-science references

nodes.definition: Decide whether a swap is a true 1:1 drop-in or a functional substitution that must rebalance structure, moisture, and leavening before any other change.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new substitution result or formula revision

pros.claim: Anchors every downstream swap to the ingredient's real function not its name
pros.example: replacing sugar treats bulk and moisture not just sweetness

cons.claim: Treating a functional swap as 1:1 silently breaks crumb and rise
cons.example: 1:1 oil for butter floods batter with fat and kills structure

failure_modes: ignoring secondary roles like moisture or browning
acceptance_tests: each swap classified 1:1 or functional with named functions
rebalance plan exists for every functional swap
revisit_triggers: crumb defect traced to unbalanced swap

nodes.definition: Build a gluten-free flour blend (starch + whole-grain + protein flour) that mimics wheat structure for the target cupcake crumb.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new substitution result or formula revision

pros.claim: A balanced blend restores wheat-like structure and avoids gritty or gummy crumb
pros.example: sorghum+rice+tapioca gives tender crumb close to cake flour

cons.claim: Single-flour swaps give gritty, dense, or beany results
cons.example: 100% rice flour bakes gritty and dry

failure_modes: gritty mouthfeel from coarse rice flour
gummy center from too much starch
acceptance_tests: blend specifies starch and whole-grain proportions

nodes.definition: Dose hydrocolloid binders (xanthan or psyllium) to replace gluten's gas-holding and elasticity without turning the crumb gummy.

included: binder dose per cup of flour

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new substitution result or formula revision

pros.claim: Correct binder dose holds gas and gives sliceable, non-crumbly crumb
pros.example: 0.5 tsp xanthan per cup blend restores cohesion

cons.claim: Overdosing binder makes gummy, heavy, or soapy-textured cupcakes
cons.example: too much xanthan gives a dense gluey center

acceptance_tests: binder dose specified per cup of flour

nodes.definition: Match the egg's specific role (bind, leaven, emulsify, moisten) to the right replacer (aquafaba, flax, commercial) per recipe.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new substitution result or formula revision

pros.claim: Matching the egg's dominant role keeps structure and rise intact
pros.example: aquafaba whips to replace egg-white aeration in light cupcakes

cons.claim: A generic egg swap fails when the egg's real job was leavening or binding
cons.example: flax egg binds but cannot aerate an angel-style crumb

failure_modes: dense gummy crumb when binding swap used for aeration role
off-flavor from flax in delicate flavors

nodes.definition: Whip and fold aquafaba to carry air as an egg-white replacer while protecting the foam from fat and over-folding.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new substitution result or formula revision

pros.claim: Stable aquafaba foam lightens vegan cupcakes without egg
pros.example: reduced aquafaba whips to stiff peaks for an airy crumb

cons.claim: Foam deflates if it contacts fat or is over-folded
cons.example: oily bowl prevents aquafaba from peaking

acceptance_tests: fold preserves at least target volume

nodes.definition: Hydrate ground flax or chia into a mucilage binder for moisture and cohesion in sturdier, darker-flavored cupcakes.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new substitution result or formula revision

pros.claim: Flax gel binds and adds moisture in robust flavors like chocolate or spice
pros.example: 1 tbsp flax + 3 tbsp water binds one egg in a spice cupcake

cons.claim: Flax adds nutty color and flavor and cannot aerate
cons.example: flax greys a vanilla crumb and weighs it down

failure_modes: dense crumb when used for lift

nodes.definition: Swap dairy butter for plant butter or solid fat while matching fat percentage, water content, and plasticity for creaming.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new substitution result or formula revision

pros.claim: A plasticity-matched plant butter creams and aerates like dairy butter
pros.example: block plant butter at 18C creams to trap air for doming

cons.claim: Higher-water spreads weaken structure and inhibit creaming
cons.example: tub spread melts during creaming and yields flat cupcakes

acceptance_tests: fat % and water content matched to butter

nodes.definition: Replace dairy milk/buttermilk with plant milk and restore acidity and protein so leavening and browning still fire.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new substitution result or formula revision

pros.claim: Acidified plant milk restores buttermilk's leavening and tenderizing role
pros.example: soy milk + lemon curdles to mimic buttermilk acidity

cons.claim: Low-protein plant milks brown poorly and read thin
cons.example: rice milk gives a pale, weak crumb

failure_modes: weak rise when buttermilk acid lost

nodes.definition: Select an alternative sweetener (liquid, sugar-alcohol, high-intensity) and rebalance bulk, moisture, and pH it no longer provides.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new substitution result or formula revision

pros.claim: Matching sugar's bulk and hygroscopy keeps texture when sweetness source changes
pros.example: honey adds moisture and browning; reduce other liquid to compensate

cons.claim: Intense sweeteners leave a bulk and moisture hole that dries the crumb
cons.example: stevia alone gives a dry, shrunken cupcake

failure_modes: dry crumb from missing sugar bulk
acceptance_tests: bulk and liquid rebalanced for chosen sweetener

nodes.definition: Predict and offset the structural effects of cutting total sugar: less tenderizing, less moisture retention, faster set, paler tops.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new substitution result or formula revision

pros.claim: Knowing sugar's structural roles caps how much can be cut before texture fails
pros.example: cutting >25% sugar toughens crumb and pales tops

cons.claim: Naive sugar cuts produce dry, tough, pale, fast-staling cupcakes
cons.example: halving sugar without compensation gives a bready cupcake

failure_modes: pale tops from lost Maillard sugar

nodes.definition: Choose an alternative fat (oil, fruit puree, nut butter) and rebalance aeration, tenderness, and moisture against the original solid fat.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new substitution result or formula revision

pros.claim: Oil maximizes moisture; fruit puree cuts fat but must offset lost tenderness
pros.example: applesauce replaces part of the oil for a lighter cupcake

cons.claim: Liquid fat cannot cream so rise relies on chemical leavening alone
cons.example: oil-based batter needs more baking powder for lift

failure_modes: dense crumb when creaming aeration is lost
rubbery crumb from over-pureed fat swap
acceptance_tests: aeration source identified when fat cannot cream

nodes.definition: Handle the top allergens (egg, dairy, wheat, nut, soy) by isolating cross-contact and verifying every component is compliant.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new substitution result or formula revision

pros.claim: Component-level allergen mapping prevents a dangerous miss
pros.example: verifying nut-free chocolate chips closes a hidden cross-contact path

cons.claim: A single unverified component can make an otherwise compliant cupcake unsafe
cons.example: 'may contain nuts' sprinkles void a nut-free claim

failure_modes: hidden allergen in a flavor or color
acceptance_tests: every component allergen-checked against exclusion list

nodes.definition: Enforce food-safety limits on raw or perishable substitute ingredients (raw flour, raw aquafaba handling, dairy/plant-milk temperature) over any flavor or texture goal.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new substitution result or formula revision

pros.claim: Safety limits prevent illness from raw flour or temperature-abused dairy swaps
pros.example: heat-treating GF flour kills pathogens before any taste-testing

cons.claim: Flavor or convenience choices that ignore the danger zone create real hazard
cons.example: leaving plant-milk batter at room temp invites spoilage

failure_modes: untreated raw flour in tasting batter
acceptance_tests: raw components heat-treated or excluded from tasting

nodes.definition: Diagnose how a chosen substitution shifts gluten/protein structure and rise, then adjust leavening, mixing, or binder to hit target crumb.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new substitution result or formula revision

pros.claim: Predicting structure delta lets you pre-adjust leavening for the right rise
pros.example: GF + vegan batch needs more leavening and a binder to dome

cons.claim: Unadjusted swaps yield flat, dense, or collapsed cupcakes
cons.example: oil + GF blend sinks without binder and extra powder

acceptance_tests: structure delta estimated for the swap stack

nodes.definition: Rebalance total moisture and water activity after a swap so cupcakes are neither dry nor gummy and stale acceptably.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new substitution result or formula revision

pros.claim: Accounting for each swap's moisture keeps crumb tender and slows staling
pros.example: honey's hygroscopy lets you cut other liquid and keep cupcakes moist

cons.claim: Stacked swaps can over- or under-hydrate, giving gummy or dry crumb
cons.example: oil + applesauce + flax over-hydrates to a gummy center

failure_modes: fast staling from low water retention
acceptance_tests: net moisture delta computed across swaps

nodes.definition: Restore Maillard/caramelization and crumb color after sugar, dairy, or egg swaps by adjusting reducing sugars, pH, and protein.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new substitution result or formula revision

pros.claim: Adding reducing sugar or a touch of soda restores golden tops lost to swaps
pros.example: a little baking soda raises pH and deepens GF cupcake color

cons.claim: Sugar and protein swaps mute Maillard, leaving pale, bland tops
cons.example: intense-sweetener + plant-milk tops stay pale and read underbaked

acceptance_tests: browning source restored when swap removes it

nodes.definition: Manage flavor changes a substitution introduces (beany, nutty, bitter, mineral) by masking, pairing, or reselecting the substitute.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new substitution result or formula revision

pros.claim: Pairing flavors to a substitute's profile turns an off-note into a feature
pros.example: chickpea note hides under cocoa in a vegan chocolate cupcake

cons.claim: Unmanaged off-flavors make the cupcake taste 'diet' or compromised
cons.example: beany aquafaba note shows through a delicate vanilla

nodes.definition: Adapt frosting for the same diet (vegan/GF/reduced-sugar) and balance its sweetness against the cake so the pair is not cloying.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new substitution result or formula revision

pros.claim: Balancing frosting sweetness against the cake avoids a cloying whole
pros.example: less-sweet cake pairs with a tangy vegan cream-cheese frosting

cons.claim: Plant-fat frostings can be soft or greasy and over-sweet if not rebalanced
cons.example: coconut-oil frosting melts and over-sweetens a sweet cake

failure_modes: greasy soft frosting from plant fat

nodes.definition: Run a controlled test bake comparing the substituted formula against a reference to confirm crumb, rise, moisture, and flavor before locking the recipe.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new substitution result or formula revision

pros.claim: A side-by-side test bake catches defects before the recipe is locked
pros.example: control vs GF-vegan batch exposes a gummy center to fix

cons.claim: Skipping the control bake hides whether the swap actually matched target
cons.example: no reference means crumb regression goes unnoticed

acceptance_tests: test bake compared against a reference control

nodes.definition: Document the final substituted formula, allergen claims, and rebalance rationale so the recipe is reproducible and claims are defensible.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new substitution result or formula revision

pros.claim: A documented formula with claims makes the cupcake reproducible and defensible
pros.example: recipe card states 'vegan, gluten-free, made on shared equipment'

cons.claim: Undocumented swaps or vague claims create reproducibility and trust risk
cons.example: missing allergen note misleads a sensitive customer

failure_modes: claim not backed by verified components

egg replacer depends on decomposing the egg's role
edges.risk_of_conflict: wrong replacer for the egg's job

edges.why_related: aquafaba handling applies once aeration role is chosen
flax binder applies once binding role is chosen

sweetener choice follows from mapping sugar's many roles
reduced-sugar limits depend on the chosen sweetener system

allergen control scopes which substitutes are even allowed
safety limits scope handling of raw substitutes
structure diagnosis uses the binder choice as input
structure diagnosis uses the egg-replacer choice
structure diagnosis accounts for whether fat can cream
edges.example: fat role known before structure tuning

edges.why_related: moisture balance depends on the sweetener's hygroscopy
moisture balance depends on the fat swap
browning restoration depends on reducing-sugar content of sweetener
browning depends on milk protein for Maillard
flavor management depends on the blend's flour flavors
flavor management depends on sweetener aftertaste
test bake validates the structure adjustments
test bake validates moisture balance
test bake proceeds only on allergen-cleared components
test bake tasting requires safety clearance
documentation records the validated formula
claims depend on verified allergen components
frosting fat swap uses plant-butter selection
frosting sweetness swap uses sweetener selection
cutting sugar directly reduces Maillard browning
edges.example: browning aid added when sugar cut

edges.why_related: cutting sugar reduces water retention and speeds staling
test results feed back to re-tune structure adjustments
edges.resolution_rule: test scorecard drives at most the protocol's max iteration passes

edges.why_related: both replace egg but for opposite roles (aerate vs bind)
adding moisture for tenderness weakens structure and rise
edges.resolution_rule: if structure fails, structure dominates and moisture is trimmed; food safety overrides both

edges.why_related: less sugar lifts flavor complexity but can read flat or sour
edges.resolution_rule: if cupcake reads unbalanced, restore minimum sweetness for acceptance

edges.why_related: intense sweeteners cut bulk sugar that drives browning
edges.example: add reducing sugar or accept paler top
edges.resolution_rule: if color target missed, add browning aid; never raise pH past safe range

edges.why_related: a less-sweet cake can clash with a standard sweet frosting
edges.resolution_rule: balance cake and frosting sweetness as a pair, not in isolation

edges.why_related: allergen exclusions can remove the best flavor-fix ingredient
edges.resolution_rule: allergen safety overrides flavor; pick a compliant alternative or accept the flavor limit

edges.why_related: tasting raw substitutes for feedback conflicts with safety limits
edges.resolution_rule: food safety overrides the desire to taste; heat-treat or exclude raw components first

edges.why_related: softer plant fats trade creaming aeration for convenience
edges.resolution_rule: if doming fails, prefer a creaming-grade fat over a convenient spread

conflict_axes.trigger: added liquid or oil for moisture weakens crumb and risks collapse
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: if crumb collapses, structure dominates and moisture is reduced
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: sunken center or gummy band observed
conflict_axes.example: oil+applesauce GF batch sinks in the middle

conflict_axes.trigger: extra fat/oil for tenderness suppresses gluten/protein and flattens domes
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: if domes flatten below target, rise dominates and fat is capped
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: dome height drops more than target

conflict_axes.trigger: cutting sugar exposes complexity but can read flat, sour, or bitter
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: if pair reads unbalanced, minimum sweetness is restored
conflict_axes.example: 75% sugar cupcake tastes sour with the acid swap

conflict_axes.trigger: reduced-sugar cake paired with standard frosting becomes cloying or mismatched
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: combined sweetness governs; the pair is balanced as a unit
conflict_axes.example: less-sweet cake under very sweet buttercream

conflict_axes.trigger: convenient drop-in swaps skip rebalancing and test bakes, hurting quality
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: if quality target missed, the rebalance/test path dominates convenience
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: scorecard below threshold without a test bake
conflict_axes.example: tub-spread drop-in skips creaming and flattens cupcakes

conflict_axes.trigger: reduced sugar and some swaps speed staling, trading day-one texture for keeping quality
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: if shelf-life target unmet, hygroscopic moisture aid is added
conflict_axes.example: low-sugar cupcake dries by next day

conflict_axes.trigger: the best flavor or texture fix may be an excluded allergen or unsafe raw component
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: safety always dominates; only compliant fixes are allowed
conflict_axes.example: nut butter would fix flavor but is excluded

conflict_axes.trigger: non-reducing or reduced sugar starves Maillard, leaving pale tops
resolution_order: add reducing sugar or soda within limits
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: if color target missed and safe, browning aid is added; pH stays in safe range

conflict_axes.trigger: more binder improves cohesion but can turn the crumb gummy or heavy
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: if gummy, minimum-effective binder dose dominates
conflict_axes.example: extra xanthan gives a gluey center

edge_cases.trigger: a flavoring, color, or topping carries a hidden or shared-equipment allergen
edge_cases.failure_mode: compliant-looking cupcake actually contains an allergen
edge_cases.example: 'may contain nuts' sprinkles void a nut-free claim

edge_cases.trigger: raw GF flour or batter tasted for feedback before heat treatment
edge_cases.example: tasting raw GF batter to check sweetness
resolution: heat-treat flour or exclude raw tasting

edge_cases.trigger: trace fat contacts whipped aquafaba and the foam collapses
edge_cases.failure_mode: lost aeration gives flat dense cupcakes

edge_cases.trigger: binder dose too high for the blend
edge_cases.example: extra xanthan gives a gluey center

edge_cases.trigger: stacked moist swaps (oil + puree + flax) over-hydrate the batter
high-intensity sweetener leaves a large bulk and moisture hole
edge_cases.example: stevia-only batch bakes dry and small

edge_cases.trigger: sugar alcohols add cooling or laxative-threshold off-notes at high dose
non-reducing or reduced sugar plus low-protein milk gives no browning
resolution: add reducing sugar or a pinch of soda

edge_cases.trigger: high-water tub spread melts during creaming
edge_cases.example: tub spread weeps water while creaming

edge_cases.trigger: coconut-oil or soft plant fat frosting slumps at room temperature
edge_cases.failure_mode: frosting melts and over-sweetens the pair
edge_cases.example: coconut-oil frosting slides off warm cupcakes
resolution: use higher-melt plant fat or stabilizer

edge_cases.trigger: aquafaba or chickpea-based swap leaves a beany note in a delicate flavor
diet/allergen claim documented without verifying every component

workflow.objective: classify each swap (1:1 vs functional), set diet/allergen exclusions, and fix safety limits
workflow.do_first_because: all downstream rebalancing and safety depends on a clear swap plan and exclusions

workflow.objective: design GF blend and dose binders to mimic wheat structure
workflow.do_first_because: GF structure base must exist before tuning rise and moisture

workflow.objective: select egg, fat, and butter replacers matched to their functions
acceptance_tests: each replacer matched to its role
workflow.do_first_because: structure and moisture tuning need the replacer choices fixed first

workflow.objective: swap dairy liquids and select/limit sweeteners with bulk and pH rebalanced
workflow.do_first_because: sweetener and dairy choices drive moisture and browning tuning

workflow.objective: diagnose structure delta from the swap stack and adjust leavening/mixing
workflow.do_first_because: structure must be tuned before moisture and browning are finalized

workflow.objective: rebalance net moisture and water activity across the swap stack
workflow.do_first_because: moisture balance depends on a fixed structure plan

workflow.objective: restore browning and manage off-flavors from the swaps
workflow.do_first_because: color and flavor are tuned once structure and moisture are stable

workflow.objective: adapt frosting to the diet and balance its sweetness against the cake
workflow.do_first_because: frosting is balanced against the finalized cake sweetness

workflow.objective: run a controlled test bake against a reference and score crumb/rise/moisture/flavor
workflow.do_first_because: the formula is only locked after a side-by-side validation bake

workflow.objective: document the final formula, allergen/diet claims, and rebalance rationale
workflow.do_first_because: a reproducible, defensible recipe record closes the workflow

dominance_rules.trigger: raw/perishable substitute or temperature abuse vs flavor/texture goal
dominance_rules.rule: food safety overrides all flavor and texture goals
dominance_rules.required_action: heat-treat or exclude unsafe components before any tasting
dominance_rules.example: raw GF batter is not tasted for sweetness until baked

dominance_rules.trigger: an excluded allergen would best fix flavor or texture
dominance_rules.required_action: reject the non-compliant fix and select a compliant alternative
dominance_rules.example: nut butter would improve flavor but is excluded, so it is rejected

dominance_rules.trigger: moisture or tenderness additions cause collapse
dominance_rules.rule: if the crumb collapses, structure dominates and moisture/fat is trimmed
dominance_rules.required_action: reduce added liquid/fat or add binder until structure holds
dominance_rules.example: trim oil and add binder when a GF-vegan batch sinks

dominance_rules.trigger: tenderizing fat flattens domes below target
dominance_rules.rule: if domes flatten below target, rise dominates and tenderizing fat is capped
dominance_rules.required_action: cap fat or add leavening to restore doming
dominance_rules.example: cap oil and add baking powder when cupcakes bake flat

dominance_rules.trigger: reduced-sugar cupcake reads flat or sour
dominance_rules.rule: if the pair reads unbalanced, minimum acceptable sweetness is restored over the reduction target
dominance_rules.required_action: restore sweetness toward the acceptance floor
dominance_rules.example: raise sugar back up when a 75% cut tastes sour

dominance_rules.rule: the cake-frosting pair's combined sweetness governs over tuning either in isolation
dominance_rules.required_action: balance cake and frosting sweetness together
dominance_rules.example: lower frosting sweetness to match a less-sweet cake

dominance_rules.trigger: convenient drop-in skips rebalancing or test bake
dominance_rules.rule: if quality target is missed, the rebalance-and-test path overrides convenience
dominance_rules.required_action: rebalance functional swaps and run a control test bake
dominance_rules.example: do not ship a tub-spread drop-in that flattened cupcakes

dominance_rules.trigger: formula changed after any swap without a control bake
dominance_rules.rule: a substituted formula is not locked until validated against a reference
dominance_rules.required_action: run the side-by-side test bake before locking
dominance_rules.example: block recipe lock until the control comparison passes

anti_rework_rules.rule: classify every swap (1:1 vs functional) before any rebalancing
anti_rework_rules.rationale: rebalancing depends on knowing each ingredient's real function
anti_rework_rules.example: adjusting leavening before mapping the egg's role

anti_rework_rules.rule: fix allergen exclusions and safety limits before selecting substitutes
anti_rework_rules.rationale: a substitute chosen against the wrong exclusion list must be redone
anti_rework_rules.example: picking nut milk before confirming nut-free

anti_rework_rules.rule: fix the GF blend before dosing binders
anti_rework_rules.rationale: binder dose only makes sense against a fixed blend
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: binder dosed against an undecided blend
anti_rework_rules.example: tuning xanthan before the flour mix is set

anti_rework_rules.rule: choose egg/fat replacers by role before aeration/binding handling
anti_rework_rules.rationale: handling work is wasted if the wrong replacer was chosen
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: whipping aquafaba for a binding role
anti_rework_rules.example: aerating when the egg only needed to bind

anti_rework_rules.rule: set sweetener and sugar level before browning tuning
anti_rework_rules.rationale: browning fixes depend on the final reducing-sugar content
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: tuning browning before sugar is fixed
anti_rework_rules.example: adding soda before the sugar cut is decided

anti_rework_rules.rule: tune structure before final moisture balance
anti_rework_rules.rationale: moisture targets shift once leavening and binder are set
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: balancing moisture before structure is fixed
anti_rework_rules.example: adding liquid before leavening is adjusted

anti_rework_rules.rule: validate with a control bake before documenting the recipe
anti_rework_rules.rationale: documenting an unvalidated formula causes rework when it fails
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: writing the recipe card before the test bake
anti_rework_rules.example: claiming success without a reference comparison

anti_rework_rules.rule: verify every component before writing an allergen/diet claim
anti_rework_rules.rationale: an unverified claim must be retracted and reworked

iteration_protocol.trigger: crumb too dry or gummy in test bake
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: moisture score meets target or max passes reached
flavor accepted or max passes reached
color acceptable or max passes reached
